description: psa-apm EXTENSION PACK — the concrete workspace vocabulary that instantiates `frontmatter-core.schema.json` (core@1) for the psa-apm workspace. Supplies the six required fields + their fix-tier authorship, the description caps by file_class, the ordered namespace vocabulary with cardinalities/parents/report-only flags, the report rules + period regex, the file_class classification globs, and the generated/exempt taxonomy. INPUT: consumed together with core@1 by the Rust validator (M2.P2.T1b) and the refitted stdlib Python gate (M2.P2.T3/T4). INVARIANT: the `namespaces` array order is significant (see its note) — it mirrors schema.py's constant declaration order so both validators emit identical code+field sequences (SC6 parity). A foreign repo adopts core@1 unchanged and ships its OWN pack in place of this one (declared via the `navigator.toml` sentinel, M3.P2.T1). Every value is traceable to `audit_helper/schema.py` or CLAUDE.md via its `source` field.

required_fields.source: schema.py:62; CLAUDE.md frontmatter table (name Required). Human-authored: a semantic title.
schema.py:62; CLAUDE.md frontmatter table (description Required, capped by class). Human-authored: routing prose (capped, see description_caps).
schema.py:62; CLAUDE.md frontmatter table (id Required, `doc-type:domain:slug`). Human-authored: identity, not mechanically inferable.
schema.py:62; CLAUDE.md frontmatter table (tags Required). Human-authored: classification judgement (Tier-1 can only repair structure, not choose topics).
schema.py:62; CLAUDE.md frontmatter table (links Required, related ids). Human-authored: relationship judgement.
schema.py:62; CLAUDE.md frontmatter table (updated Required, ISO-8601 UTC). Machine_derivable: stampable at fix time (Tier-1).

description_caps.source: CLAUDE.md frontmatter table — description length cap by file class (context/workspace ≤350, Skills ≤500, Agents ≤750).

rules.source: CLAUDE.md `.claude/skills/` — each skill is a `SKILL.md`; ≤500-char description class.
CLAUDE.md — any `SKILL.md` anywhere is a skill (broad fallback after the anchored rule).
CLAUDE.md `.claude/agents/` — one `.md` per subagent; ≤750-char description class.

file_class.note: Rules evaluated in array order, first match wins, else `default`. Globs use fnmatch semantics (`*` spans `/`); the anchored skill rule precedes the broad `**/SKILL.md` so both a nested and a repo-root SKILL.md classify as skill. `default=context` covers all workspace/context/knowledge/report docs (the ≤350 class). NEW classification (no schema.py equivalent) — see DIVERGENCES.md.

namespaces.source: NEW — CLAUDE.md `owner:` exactly one (repo-split routing key). ABSENT from schema.py SINGLE_VALUE_NAMESPACES. Appended AFTER privacy so the shared codes' emission order is unchanged for pre-owner files. See DIVERGENCES.md.

namespaces.name: topic
namespaces.source: schema.py:72 AT_LEAST_ONE_NAMESPACES; CLAUDE.md `topic:` one or more.

namespaces.name: feature
namespaces.source: schema.py:78-81 NAMESPACE_PARENTS (feature→(product,suite)); CLAUDE.md feature requires product+suite. Ordered BEFORE product to preserve schema.py dict-iteration order (feature resolved first).

namespaces.name: product
namespaces.source: schema.py:78-81 NAMESPACE_PARENTS (product→(suite,)); CLAUDE.md product requires suite.

namespaces.name: period
namespaces.source: schema.py:84 REPORT_ONLY_NAMESPACES; CLAUDE.md `period:` report-only + report-required, format-validated. `type: date_interval` — a downstream range-eligibility consumer (facetquery) treats this facet's value as a closed date range and matches on OVERLAP against a query window (or a single-day window), not equality or single-point comparison.

namespaces.name: cadence
namespaces.source: schema.py:84 REPORT_ONLY_NAMESPACES; CLAUDE.md `cadence:` report-only, defaults to on-demand when unspecified (NOT report-required).

namespaces_order_note: Array order IS the cascade iteration order (core `violation_cascade`). It reproduces schema.py's constant order exactly: singletons type,status,privacy (+owner appended, DIVERGENCE); at_least_one topic; parents feature-then-product (schema.py dict order, so ORPHAN emits for feature before product); report_only source,period,audience,cadence (schema.py:84 tuple order). `suite`/`team` are order-inert optionals placed to keep related namespaces adjacent. Reordering this array changes SC6 parity output — do not reorder without regenerating the M2.P2.T2 frozen goldens.

report.notes: `cadence` defaults to on-demand when unspecified and is NOT required; `audience` is optional. `period` is `type: date_interval`, ISO 8601 interval form (`YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD`, single `/` separator, both endpoints inclusive) — Stage 2 of the interval migration off schema.py's legacy `..`-separated PERIOD_RE (schema.py:91); the live Python gate adopts the same `/` form separately (Stage 3), so this pack is no longer byte-identical to today's schema.py on `period` values, by design. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE (carried from M2.P2.T1b finalization, still applies): uses explicit ASCII `[0-9]` rather than `\d`, because the Rust validator compiles this string with the `regex` crate, whose `\d` matches any Unicode decimal digit by default — `[0-9]` is ASCII-only regardless of that flag, rejecting e.g. Arabic-Indic digits that an un-flagged Python `\d` would otherwise accept.

exempt.source: schema.py:200-223 — DOC_EXEMPT_FILENAMES / DOC_EXEMPT_DIR_COMPONENTS / DOC_EXEMPT_PATH_GLOBS ported verbatim (same values, same order).
